```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern unit-of-work
 * @options 0068972a660b0e04
 */

/**
 * A unit of work: changes accumulate here and are written in one commit.
 *
 * Nothing here mentions a domain type. This module is the machinery every
 * entity shares; each entity gets a small binding of its own that supplies its
 * record constraint and collection name.
 *
 * Changes are declared. Each tracked record has an `update` method taking a
 * patch, so a change cannot be missed and nothing is copied. The patch type
 * excludes the key field, which makes changing a record's identity a compile
 * error rather than a surprise at commit.
 *
 * Every record carries a `version`, and every write is conditional on the value
 * that was loaded. If another unit of work got there first the whole commit
 * fails, with the record named, and nothing is written. Some such check is the
 * only defence available: reads happen before the commit, so they are not
 * inside it.
 *
 * `Store` is the seam, and it takes a *batch* rather than handing out a
 * transaction. That is what makes it implementable on a datastore with no
 * interactive transaction, and it keeps a connection from being held open while
 * domain code runs. Applying a batch atomically is the adapter's half of the
 * contract; `createMemoryStore` is a complete implementation that honours it.
 *
 * There is no `rollback`, because there is nothing to roll back: nothing has
 * been written before `commit`, so abandoning a unit of work is how a
 * transaction is discarded.
 */

/**
 * A record as this module holds it: fields by name, its type forgotten.
 *
 * One table holds the records of every collection, and a table keyed by strings
 * cannot know that `orders` holds orders. So the type is dropped here and
 * asserted again where a record is handed back — two halves of one unsoundness,
 * in two named places, rather than scattered through the file.
 */
export type Fields = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

function fieldsOf(record: object): Fields {
  return record as Fields;
}

/**
 * What a versioned record carries beyond its key.
 *
 * This module owns the field: it is assigned on insert, incremented on update,
 * and set from what was stored when a commit succeeds. A value a caller writes
 * to it does not survive.
 */
export interface Versioned {
  readonly version: number;
}

/**
 * The least a record must be for this module to track it: a string-valued field
 * holding its key.
 *
 * Constraining the record rather than the field is what keeps this file free of
 * casts. `keyof T` filtered to its string-valued members names the right fields
 * and leaves `T[F]` unreducible, so reading a key would need an assertion;
 * written this way, `record[spec.keyField]` is an ordinary indexed access.
 */
export type Storable<F extends string> = Readonly<Record<F, string>> &
  Versioned;

/**
 * What a binding tells this module about one collection.
 *
 * `keyField` is the field's *name*, as a type parameter, which is what lets a
 * patch type exclude it and a key be read without a cast.
 *
 * Keys are strings because a record must have its key before it is inserted:
 * the identity map is keyed on it, and a key the datastore assigns is not known
 * until after the write, by which time nothing in the same transaction could
 * have referred to the new record. A sequence-assigned integer key therefore
 * cannot participate, and saying so is better than appearing to support it.
 */
declare const ENTITY: unique symbol;

export interface CollectionSpec<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string> {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly keyField: F;
  /**
   * Phantom: never read, never written, never present at run time. Without it,
   * two collections keyed on a field of the same name are the same type, so a
   * function annotated for one would accept the other's spec and hand back
   * records of the wrong type.
   */
  readonly [ENTITY]?: T;
}

/**
 * The fields of a tracked record that may be changed.
 *
 * The key field is absent, so changing a record's identity is a compile error.
 * It has to be: applying it would mean either a second record under the new key
 * or a silent delete of the old one, and neither is what the line said.
 * `version` is absent for the reason given above — this module owns it.
 *
 * Written out rather than as `Partial<Omit<…>>` so that every field admits an
 * explicit `undefined`, which `Partial` alone does not under
 * `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. A caller spreading a form or a partial DTO
 * produces exactly that, and `update` is documented to treat it as no change —
 * so it has to be sayable, or the same code would compile under one
 * configuration and not another.
 */
export type Patch<T, F extends string> = {
  [K in keyof Omit<T, F | "version">]?: T[K] | undefined;
};

/**
 * A record on its way in, before this module has given it a version.
 *
 * The intersection restates the key requirement because `Omit` leaves the
 * compiler unable to see it: `F` is a bare `string` there, so as far as the
 * type system knows it could name the field just removed.
 */
export type NewRecord<T, F extends string> = Omit<T, "version"> &
  Readonly<Record<F, string>>;

/**
 * A record this unit of work is watching.
 *
 * A plain record is not one of these, which is the point: a function that means
 * to change something persistently can say so in its parameter type, and be
 * handed a record nobody is watching only over a compile error.
 */
export interface Tracked<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string> {
  /**
   * The record as it stands, including every change made through `update`.
   */
  readonly value: T;
  /**
   * Record a change. Merging rather than replacing, so two callers each
   * changing one field do not undo each other. An `undefined` value is not a
   * change and does not erase the field: erasing one has to be said in the
   * domain type, with a `null` or an absent-marker of its own, because a patch
   * cannot tell "leave it alone" from "clear it".
   */
  update(changes: Patch<T, F>): void;
  /**
   * Mark this record for deletion. Idempotent, and a record added in this unit
   * of work leaves the plan entirely rather than becoming an insert followed by
   * a delete of something never written.
   */
  remove(): void;
}

/**
 * One write, as the store receives it.
 *
 * Insert, update and delete rather than one upsert, because the three have
 * different failure conditions and an adapter that cannot tell them apart
 * cannot report which one it was: an insert onto an occupied key and a delete
 * of a key that has gone are both mistakes, and an upsert hides them both.
 */
export type Operation =
  | {
      readonly kind: "insert";
      readonly collection: string;
      readonly key: string;
      readonly record: Fields;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "update";
      readonly collection: string;
      readonly key: string;
      readonly record: Fields;
      /**
       * The version the record held when it was loaded. The write must not
       * happen if the stored value has moved.
       */
      readonly expectedVersion: number;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "delete";
      readonly collection: string;
      readonly key: string;
      /**
       * The version the record held when it was loaded. The write must not
       * happen if the stored value has moved.
       */
      readonly expectedVersion: number;
    };

/**
 * The datastore seam: implement once per datastore, share across every unit of
 * work.
 *
 * `read` is generic in the record type, which means the implementation is
 * trusted to return the shape the collection holds — the unsoundness every
 * persistence boundary has, confined here on purpose.
 *
 * `apply` receives the whole batch and must apply all of it or none of it. That
 * is the contract, and it is the one this pattern rests on: a half-applied
 * commit is the failure a unit of work exists to prevent, and no amount of care
 * above this line can prevent it if the line below does not hold.
 */
export interface Store {
  read<T>(collection: string, key: string): Promise<T | undefined>;
  apply(batch: readonly Operation[]): Promise<void>;
}

/**
 * A record that had to exist did not.
 *
 * Thrown by `require` and not by `load`: a lookup that may legitimately find
 * nothing returns `undefined`, and one whose caller has already decided the
 * record must be there gets an error naming what was missing.
 */
export class RecordNotFoundError extends Error {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly key: string;

  constructor(collection: string, key: string) {
    super(`No record in "${collection}" with key "${key}".`);
    this.name = "RecordNotFoundError";
    this.collection = collection;
    this.key = key;
  }
}

/**
 * `add` was given a key this unit of work is already watching.
 *
 * Refused rather than merged, because the two plausible meanings differ: adding
 * a record that was loaded is an update written as an insert, and adding one
 * twice is a duplicate. Neither is worth guessing at.
 */
export class AlreadyTrackedError extends Error {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly key: string;

  constructor(collection: string, key: string) {
    super(
      `"${key}" in "${collection}" is already tracked by this unit of work.`,
    );
    this.name = "AlreadyTrackedError";
    this.collection = collection;
    this.key = key;
  }
}

/**
 * A record was changed after being marked for deletion.
 *
 * Refused, because no order of the two operations does what the code appears to
 * say: the delete either discards the change or resurrects the record.
 */
export class RemovedRecordError extends Error {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly key: string;

  constructor(collection: string, key: string) {
    super(
      `"${key}" in "${collection}" was removed in this unit of work, so it cannot be updated.`,
    );
    this.name = "RemovedRecordError";
    this.collection = collection;
    this.key = key;
  }
}

/**
 * Another writer got there first.
 *
 * Thrown by the store while applying a batch, and exported so that every
 * adapter reports a conflict the same way. Nothing in the batch has been
 * written when this arrives, which is what makes retrying the whole transaction
 * the right response to it.
 */
export class ConcurrencyError extends Error {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly key: string;

  constructor(collection: string, key: string) {
    super(`Record "${key}" in "${collection}" changed since it was loaded.`);
    this.name = "ConcurrencyError";
    this.collection = collection;
    this.key = key;
  }
}

/**
 * The unit of work has already been committed.
 *
 * Every method refuses rather than proceeding, because the alternative is a
 * change that is silently never written — indistinguishable from success until
 * the record is read back somewhere else. A committed unit of work is finished;
 * open another.
 */
export class UnitOfWorkClosedError extends Error {
  constructor(action: string) {
    super(
      `This unit of work has been committed, so ${action} would never be written. ` +
        "Open another for the next transaction.",
    );
    this.name = "UnitOfWorkClosedError";
  }
}

/** One record this unit of work is watching, as it is held internally. */
interface Registration {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly keyField: string;
  readonly key: string;
  state: "new" | "loaded" | "removed";
  record: Fields;
  changed: boolean;
  loadedVersion: number;
  /**
   * Handed back on every later load of the same key, so two parts of one
   * transaction cannot hold different copies of one record.
   */
  handle: unknown;
}

/**
 * Changes accumulate here; `commit` writes them.
 *
 * One instance per business transaction. It is not a cache: the identity map
 * exists so that two parts of one transaction agree with each other, and
 * holding one open across transactions would mean serving records loaded
 * arbitrarily long ago.
 */
export class UnitOfWork {
  private readonly registrations = new Map<string, Registration>();
  private readonly sequence: Registration[] = [];
  private closed = false;

  constructor(private readonly store: Store) {}

  /**
   * The record under this key, tracked, or `undefined` if there is none.
   *
   * A record this unit of work has already loaded or added comes back without
   * the store being touched, and one it has removed reads as absent — so a
   * transaction sees its own changes, which is the difference between a unit of
   * work and a series of unrelated calls.
   */
  async load<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
    spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
    key: T[F],
  ): Promise<Tracked<T, F> | undefined> {
    this.assertOpen("loading a record");

    const known = this.registrations.get(slotFor(spec.collection, key));
    if (known !== undefined) {
      return known.state === "removed"
        ? undefined
        : this.handleFor<T, F>(known);
    }

    const record = await this.store.read<T>(spec.collection, key);
    if (record === undefined) {
      return undefined;
    }

    return this.handleFor<T, F>(
      this.register({
        collection: spec.collection,
        keyField: spec.keyField,
        key,
        state: "loaded",
        record: fieldsOf(record),
        changed: false,
        loadedVersion: record.version,
        handle: undefined,
      }),
    );
  }

  /**
   * The record under this key, tracked, or an error naming what was missing.
   *
   * @throws RecordNotFoundError when there is no such record.
   */
  async require<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
    spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
    key: T[F],
  ): Promise<Tracked<T, F>> {
    const found = await this.load<T, F>(spec, key);
    if (found === undefined) {
      throw new RecordNotFoundError(spec.collection, key);
    }
    return found;
  }

  /**
   * Track a new record, to be inserted at commit.
   *
   * A copy is taken, so the handle is what to change from here. The version is
   * assigned rather than supplied, which is why the parameter type has no
   * `version` field.
   *
   * @throws AlreadyTrackedError when this unit of work is already watching that
   * key.
   */
  add<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
    spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
    record: NewRecord<T, F>,
  ): Tracked<T, F> {
    this.assertOpen("adding a record");

    const key = record[spec.keyField];
    if (this.registrations.has(slotFor(spec.collection, key))) {
      throw new AlreadyTrackedError(spec.collection, key);
    }

    return this.handleFor<T, F>(
      this.register({
        collection: spec.collection,
        keyField: spec.keyField,
        key,
        state: "new",
        record: { ...fieldsOf(record), version: 1 },
        changed: true,
        loadedVersion: 0,
        handle: undefined,
      }),
    );
  }

  /**
   * What `commit` would write, in the order it would write it.
   *
   * Public because it is the honest answer to "is there anything to do": an
   * empty plan means no write, which is not the same as no changes having been
   * attempted. A transaction worth logging is also worth logging as the
   * operations it became.
   */
  plan(): readonly Operation[] {
    return this.planned().map((entry) => entry.operation);
  }

  /**
   * Write every accumulated change, or none of them.
   *
   * The unit of work is closed afterwards and every method on it refuses. A
   * commit that *fails* leaves it open: nothing was written, so the caller can
   * look at what happened and decide whether to try again.
   *
   * @throws ConcurrencyError by way of the store, when a record has changed
   * since it was loaded.
   *
   * @throws UnitOfWorkClosedError when this unit of work has already been
   * committed.
   */
  async commit(): Promise<void> {
    this.assertOpen("committing");

    const planned = this.planned();

    if (planned.length > 0) {
      await this.store.apply(planned.map((entry) => entry.operation));
    }

    // What was stored, written back, so that a record still in the caller's
    // hands carries the version of the row it describes rather than the one it
    // was loaded at.
    //
    // Only the record. `loadedVersion` is bookkeeping for the next write, and
    // there is no next write: this unit of work is finished below, and nothing
    // that reads that field can be reached again.
    for (const { registration, operation } of planned) {
      if (operation.kind !== "delete") {
        registration.record = operation.record;
      }
    }

    this.closed = true;
    // Nothing is pending any more, which `plan()` should say: a record that was
    // inserted is a loaded one now, a record that was deleted is gone, and a
    // change that has been written is not a change.
    for (const registration of [...this.sequence]) {
      if (registration.state === "removed") {
        this.registrations.delete(
          slotFor(registration.collection, registration.key),
        );
        this.sequence.splice(this.sequence.indexOf(registration), 1);
        continue;
      }
      registration.state = "loaded";
      registration.changed = false;
    }
  }

  private register(registration: Registration): Registration {
    this.registrations.set(
      slotFor(registration.collection, registration.key),
      registration,
    );
    this.sequence.push(registration);
    return registration;
  }

  /**
   * The handle for a registration, made once and then kept.
   *
   * The one place a record's type is asserted rather than proven, and the other
   * half of `fieldsOf`. What is trusted is that a collection name names one
   * entity type, which the phantom on `CollectionSpec` is what makes hard to
   * get wrong: a spec for one entity cannot be passed where another's is
   * expected.
   *
   * Kept rather than remade because identity is part of what this pattern
   * promises — two loads of one key are the same handle, so a change made
   * through one is visible through the other.
   */
  private handleFor<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
    registration: Registration,
  ): Tracked<T, F> {
    const existing = registration.handle;
    if (existing !== undefined) {
      return existing as Tracked<T, F>;
    }

    const handle: Tracked<T, F> = {
      get value(): T {
        return registration.record as unknown as T;
      },
      update: (changes: Patch<T, F>): void => {
        this.assertOpen("updating a record");
        if (registration.state === "removed") {
          throw new RemovedRecordError(
            registration.collection,
            registration.key,
          );
        }

        const supplied = Object.entries(changes).filter(
          ([, value]) => value !== undefined,
        );
        if (supplied.length === 0) {
          return;
        }

        registration.record = {
          ...registration.record,
          ...Object.fromEntries(supplied),
        };
        registration.changed = true;
      },
      remove: (): void => {
        this.assertOpen("removing a record");

        // A record added in this unit of work has never been written, so there
        // is nothing to delete: it leaves the plan entirely rather than
        // becoming an insert followed by a delete.
        if (registration.state === "new") {
          this.registrations.delete(
            slotFor(registration.collection, registration.key),
          );
          const at = this.sequence.indexOf(registration);
          if (at >= 0) {
            this.sequence.splice(at, 1);
          }
        }

        registration.state = "removed";
      },
    };

    registration.handle = handle;
    return handle;
  }

  /**
   * Each pending write beside the record it came from.
   *
   * Inserts, then updates, then deletes; registration order within each. A row
   * an update refers to therefore exists before the update, and a row still
   * referred to is not deleted first. Order between collections is registration
   * order and nothing cleverer — a true dependency order would need to know
   * which fields are references, which nothing here is told.
   */
  private planned(): readonly {
    registration: Registration;
    operation: Operation;
  }[] {
    const planned: { registration: Registration; operation: Operation }[] = [];

    for (const kind of ["insert", "update", "delete"] as const) {
      for (const registration of this.sequence) {
        const operation = operationFor(registration);
        if (operation !== undefined && operation.kind === kind) {
          planned.push({ registration, operation });
        }
      }
    }

    return planned;
  }

  private assertOpen(action: string): void {
    if (this.closed) {
      throw new UnitOfWorkClosedError(action);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * The single write a tracked record has become, or nothing.
 *
 * This is where the states collapse, and where the reason for collapsing them
 * shows: a record that was loaded and not changed produces *no* write. A unit
 * of work that wrote back everything it had seen would be slower and, worse,
 * would conflict with every other transaction that had merely read the same
 * record.
 */
function operationFor(registration: Registration): Operation | undefined {
  switch (registration.state) {
    case "new":
      return {
        kind: "insert",
        collection: registration.collection,
        key: registration.key,
        record: registration.record,
      };

    case "loaded": {
      if (!registration.changed) {
        return undefined;
      }

      return {
        kind: "update",
        collection: registration.collection,
        key: registration.key,
        record: {
          ...registration.record,
          version: registration.loadedVersion + 1,
        },
        expectedVersion: registration.loadedVersion,
      };
    }

    case "removed":
      return {
        kind: "delete",
        collection: registration.collection,
        key: registration.key,
        expectedVersion: registration.loadedVersion,
      };
  }
}

/**
 * The identity-map key for one record.
 *
 * A NUL separator rather than a colon, because a collection name or a key that
 * contained the separator would otherwise let two different records share a
 * slot.
 */
function slotFor(collection: string, key: string): string {
  return `${collection}\u0000${key}`;
}

/**
 * Run a transaction: open a unit of work, hand it to `run`, and commit if `run`
 * returns.
 *
 * The point is the failure path. If `run` throws, nothing is committed and
 * nothing has been written, so a transaction abandoned halfway leaves the
 * datastore as it was without anybody having to remember a rollback. Forgetting
 * to commit is the other defect this closes, and the more common one.
 */
export async function withUnitOfWork<R>(
  store: Store,
  run: (uow: UnitOfWork) => Promise<R>,
): Promise<R> {
  const uow = new UnitOfWork(store);
  const result = await run(uow);
  await uow.commit();
  return result;
}

/**
 * An insert named a key the store already holds.
 *
 * The store's error rather than the unit of work's: it is the only party that
 * knows what is there. An insert that quietly became an update is how two
 * transactions end up each believing it created the record.
 */
export class AlreadyStoredError extends Error {
  readonly collection: string;
  readonly key: string;

  constructor(collection: string, key: string) {
    super(`A record in "${collection}" already has key "${key}".`);
    this.name = "AlreadyStoredError";
    this.collection = collection;
    this.key = key;
  }
}

/**
 * A complete `Store` held in memory.
 *
 * Not a mock: it honours the whole contract, including the part that matters
 * most — every operation in a batch is checked before any of it is written, so
 * a batch that cannot be applied leaves the store exactly as it was. A suite
 * written against this exercises the unit of work rather than a stand-in for
 * it.
 *
 * `seed` and `records` are here because this seam has no read-everything
 * method: a store whose only read is by key needs a door for a test to look
 * through, and putting one on `Store` itself would make every real adapter
 * implement it.
 */
export interface MemoryStore extends Store {
  /**
   * Put records in place without going through a unit of work, for a test's
   * starting state.
   */
  seed<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
    spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
    records: readonly T[],
  ): void;
  /**
   * Everything in one collection, in insertion order. Typed by the same spec
   * that seeded it, which is the only reason it can be typed at all — the table
   * underneath has forgotten.
   */
  records<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
    spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
  ): readonly T[];
  /**
   * How many batches have been applied successfully. A test asserting that
   * nothing was written asserts on this, since an empty batch is never sent and
   * a refused one is not counted.
   */
  readonly applied: number;
}

export function createMemoryStore(): MemoryStore {
  const collections = new Map<string, Map<string, Fields>>();
  let applied = 0;

  const rowsIn = (collection: string): Map<string, Fields> => {
    const existing = collections.get(collection);
    if (existing !== undefined) {
      return existing;
    }
    const created = new Map<string, Fields>();
    collections.set(collection, created);
    return created;
  };

  return {
    get applied(): number {
      return applied;
    },

    seed<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
      spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
      records: readonly T[],
    ): void {
      const rows = rowsIn(spec.collection);
      for (const record of records) {
        rows.set(record[spec.keyField], fieldsOf(record));
      }
    },

    records<T extends Storable<F>, F extends string>(
      spec: CollectionSpec<T, F>,
    ): readonly T[] {
      return [...rowsIn(spec.collection).values()] as readonly T[];
    },

    read<T>(collection: string, key: string): Promise<T | undefined> {
      const found = rowsIn(collection).get(key);
      // A copy, so that a caller changing what it was handed cannot reach into
      // the store. A real adapter gets this for free by deserialising; an
      // in-memory one has to mean it.
      return Promise.resolve(
        found === undefined ? undefined : ({ ...found } as T),
      );
    },

    async apply(batch: readonly Operation[]): Promise<void> {
      // Every expectation first, every write second. That is the whole of what
      // "atomic" means here, and the reason the seam takes a batch rather than
      // a connection.
      for (const operation of batch) {
        const current = rowsIn(operation.collection).get(operation.key);

        if (operation.kind === "insert") {
          if (current !== undefined) {
            throw new AlreadyStoredError(operation.collection, operation.key);
          }
          continue;
        }

        if (
          current === undefined ||
          current["version"] !== operation.expectedVersion
        ) {
          throw new ConcurrencyError(operation.collection, operation.key);
        }
      }

      for (const operation of batch) {
        const rows = rowsIn(operation.collection);
        if (operation.kind === "delete") {
          rows.delete(operation.key);
        } else {
          rows.set(operation.key, operation.record);
        }
      }

      applied += 1;
      await Promise.resolve();
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The Order collection: its minimum record, its name, and a typed accessor.
 *
 * The machinery lives in `unit-of-work-core` and is shared with every other
 * entity. Adding a second entity means a second file like this one, not a

import type {
  CollectionSpec,
  NewRecord,
  Tracked,
  UnitOfWork,
} from "./unit-of-work-core.js";

/**
 * What `Order` must have for this module to track it.
 *
 * Your own `Order` satisfies this by having an `id` and a `version`, so nothing
 * here needs to know the rest of its fields. That is deliberate: a generated
 * file that declared your domain type would have to be edited every time the
 * domain changed, and regenerating it would then overwrite the edit.
 *
 * The key is a plain `string`. `branded-type` is how it stops being
 * interchangeable with every other entity's key, and the change is confined to
 * this file.
 */
export interface OrderRecord {
  readonly id: string;
  /**
   * Assigned on insert and incremented on every update by the unit of work,
   * never by you.
   */
  readonly version: number;
}

/**
 * Where Order records live.
 *
 * Exported so that a datastore adapter can be told which collections exist
 * without importing every entity's accessor.
 */
export const ORDERS_COLLECTION = "orders";

/**
 * Tracking orders in one unit of work.
 *
 * Generic in your own `Order`, so every method is typed in terms of your type
 * rather than the minimum this file declares.
 */
export interface OrderTracking<T extends OrderRecord> {
  /**
   * The record under this key, or `undefined` if there is none.
   */
  load(id: T["id"]): Promise<Tracked<T, "id"> | undefined>;
  /**
   * The record under this key, or an error naming what was missing.
   */
  require(id: T["id"]): Promise<Tracked<T, "id">>;
  /**
   * Track a new record, to be inserted at commit.
   */
  add(record: NewRecord<T, "id">): Tracked<T, "id">;
}

/**
 * What the machinery needs to know about orders, at your own record type.
 *
 * A function rather than a constant because it is specific to the `T` you use
 * it at, and a constant would have to be declared at one of them. `orders`
 * calls it, and so does anything that has to name this collection to something
 * entity-independent — an in-memory store's fixtures, for one.
 */
export function orderCollectionSpec<T extends OrderRecord>(): CollectionSpec<
  T,
  "id"
> {
  return { collection: ORDERS_COLLECTION, keyField: "id" };
}

/**
 * Track orders in `uow`.
 *
 * Pass your domain type: `orders<Order>(uow)`.
 */
export function orders<T extends OrderRecord>(
  uow: UnitOfWork,
): OrderTracking<T> {
  const spec = orderCollectionSpec<T>();

  return {
    load: (id) => uow.load<T, "id">(spec, id),
    require: (id) => uow.require<T, "id">(spec, id),
    add: (record) => uow.add<T, "id">(spec, record),
  };
}
```

## order-collection-example.ts (example)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern unit-of-work
 * @options 09e1d920d7569ceb
 */

/**
 * Using the Order collection: one transaction, one commit.
 *
 * Everything here is what a caller writes. The only thing worth watching is
 * what is *not* written: a record that was read and not changed, and a record
 * added and then removed, both cost nothing at commit.
 */

import { createMemoryStore, withUnitOfWork } from "./unit-of-work-core.js";
import type { Store, Tracked } from "./unit-of-work-core.js";

import { orderCollectionSpec, orders } from "./order-collection.js";
import type { OrderRecord, OrderTracking } from "./order-collection.js";

/**
 * Your own `Order`. The collection requires an `id` and a `version`; the rest
 * is yours.
 */
export interface Order extends OrderRecord {
  readonly total: number;
  readonly status: "open" | "paid";
}

/**
 * One business transaction: settle an order and open its follow-up.
 *
 * Both changes reach the store in a single batch, or neither does. Note the
 * third record: it is read and not changed, so it produces no write at all — a
 * unit of work that wrote back everything it had seen would conflict with every
 * other transaction that had merely read the same row.
 */
export async function settleOrders(store: Store): Promise<readonly string[]> {
  return withUnitOfWork(store, async (uow) => {
    const tracked = orders<Order>(uow);

    const paid = await tracked.require("A-1");
    paid.update({ status: "paid" });

    const followUp = tracked.add({ id: "A-2", total: 0, status: "open" });
    followUp.update({ total: 250 });

    // Read, considered, left alone.
    await tracked.load("A-3");

    // Nothing has been written yet. This is the whole of what commit will do.
    return uow.plan().map((operation) => `${operation.kind} ${operation.key}`);
  });
}

/**
 * A transaction that decides against itself halfway through.
 *
 * The change above the throw is never written, and there is no rollback to
 * forget: nothing had been written to undo.
 */
export async function abandonOrder(store: Store): Promise<string> {
  try {
    await withUnitOfWork(store, async (uow) => {
      const tracked = orders<Order>(uow);

      const order = await tracked.require("A-1");
      order.update({ total: 0 });

      throw new Error("a domain rule said no");
    });
    return "committed";
  } catch {
    return "nothing written";
  }
}

/**
 * Both of the above against an in-memory store, which is what to run before a
 * datastore exists.
 */
export async function demonstrate(): Promise<{
  readonly planned: readonly string[];
  readonly abandoned: string;
  readonly stored: number;
}> {
  const store = createMemoryStore();
  const spec = orderCollectionSpec<Order>();
  store.seed(spec, [
    { id: "A-1", total: 100, status: "open", version: 1 },
    { id: "A-3", total: 40, status: "paid", version: 7 },
  ]);

  const planned = await settleOrders(store);
  const abandoned = await abandonOrder(store);

  return { planned, abandoned, stored: store.records(spec).length };
}

/**
 * What the compiler refuses, stated as code that must not compile.
 *
 * Each directive is an assertion: if the guarantee above it lapses, the
 * directive goes unused and this file stops compiling on that instead.
 */
export function refusesImpossibleChanges(order: Tracked<Order, "id">): void {
  // @ts-expect-error the key field is absent from a patch, so identity cannot
  // change
  order.update({ id: "A-9" });

  // @ts-expect-error a field the entity does not have
  order.update({ discount: 10 });

  // @ts-expect-error the wrong type for a real field
  order.update({ total: "lots" });
}

/**
 * The version is assigned, not supplied.
 *
 * Worth asserting rather than documenting: a caller who sets it is stating a
 * fact about a record that does not exist yet, and the value they choose would
 * be silently replaced.
 */
export function refusesASuppliedVersion(tracked: OrderTracking<Order>): void {
  // The directive sits on the offending property rather than above the call: it
  // suppresses the line that follows it, and the excess property is reported
  // where it is written.
  tracked.add({
    id: "A-9",
    total: 1,
    status: "open",
    // @ts-expect-error version is not part of a new record
    version: 1,
  });
}

/**
 * A record nobody is watching is not a tracked one.
 *
 * The reason to reach for this pattern at all: a function that means to change
 * something persistently says so in its parameter type, and cannot be handed a
 * record whose changes would go nowhere.
 */
export function refusesAnUntrackedRecord(order: Order): void {
  // Written as a direct call rather than through a callback. Argument
  // assignability at a call is invariant at every strictness; a callback
  // parameter is compared bivariantly without `strictFunctionTypes`, which
  // would make this compile under a loose configuration and leave the directive
  // unused.
  //
  // @ts-expect-error a plain record has no handle, so nothing here would ever
  // be written
  refusesImpossibleChanges(order);
}
```

## order-collection.test.ts (test)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern unit-of-work
 * @options 09e1d920d7569ceb
 */

/**
 * A unit of work over orders, exercised against the in-memory store.
 *
 * Nothing here is mocked. The store is a real implementation of the seam a
 * datastore adapter implements, so a failure means the unit of work is wrong
 * rather than that a stub disagreed with it.
 */

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  AlreadyStoredError,
  AlreadyTrackedError,
  ConcurrencyError,
  RecordNotFoundError,
  RemovedRecordError,
  UnitOfWork,
  UnitOfWorkClosedError,
  createMemoryStore,
  withUnitOfWork,
} from "./unit-of-work-core.js";
import type { MemoryStore, Tracked } from "./unit-of-work-core.js";
import {
  ORDERS_COLLECTION,
  orderCollectionSpec,
  orders,
} from "./order-collection.js";
import type { OrderRecord, OrderTracking } from "./order-collection.js";

/**
 * The domain type the suite tracks, standing in for the caller's own.
 *
 * `shipping` is here because a nested field is where a change-detection rule
 * either holds or does not, and a suite of scalars would never find out.
 */
interface Order extends OrderRecord {
  readonly total: number;
  readonly status: "open" | "paid";
  readonly shipping: { city: string };
}

/**
 * A store with two records in it, and a unit of work over that store.
 *
 * The spec is the same one the accessor uses, which is what lets the store's
 * fixtures be typed as this suite's own record type rather than as bags of
 * fields.
 */
const spec = orderCollectionSpec<Order>();

function seeded(): MemoryStore {
  const store = createMemoryStore();
  store.seed(spec, [
    {
      id: "A-1",
      total: 100,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "York" },
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: "A-2",
      total: 40,
      status: "paid",
      shipping: { city: "Leeds" },
      version: 7,
    },
  ]);
  return store;
}

function opened(store: MemoryStore): {
  readonly uow: UnitOfWork;
  readonly orders: OrderTracking<Order>;
} {
  const uow = new UnitOfWork(store);
  return { uow, orders: orders<Order>(uow) };
}

function stored(store: MemoryStore, id: string): Order | undefined {
  return store.records(spec).find((row) => row.id === id);
}

/**
 * The plan as short strings, which is what most of these cases are really
 * about.
 */
function planOf(uow: UnitOfWork): readonly string[] {
  return uow.plan().map((operation) => `${operation.kind} ${operation.key}`);
}

/**
 * Whatever a call refused with.
 *
 * Handed to `toBeInstanceOf` rather than matching on the message, so the
 * assertion is about which refusal it was and not about its wording — the
 * wording is free to improve.
 */
function refusalFrom(run: () => void): unknown {
  try {
    run();
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error("expected a refusal, and the call returned");
}

/**
 * Making a change, however this bundle spells it.
 *
 * The rest of the suite is identical in both renderings, which is the point:
 * how a change is expressed is an option, what a change *means* is not.
 *
 * Reading the status is the one adapter the snapshot rendering does not need.
 * Only the merging case asks for it — a patch is a thing the explicit rendering
 * has and the snapshot one does not — and an adapter no case calls is dead
 * however symmetrical it looks.
 */
function change(
  order: Tracked<Order, "id">,
  fields: { readonly total?: number; readonly status?: "open" | "paid" },
): void {
  order.update(fields);
}

function totalOf(order: Tracked<Order, "id">): number {
  return order.value.total;
}

function statusOf(order: Tracked<Order, "id">): string {
  return order.value.status;
}

describe("what reaches the store", () => {
  it("nothing at all before commit", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    change(order, { status: "paid" });

    expect(store.applied).toBe(0);
    expect(stored(store, "A-1")?.status).toBe("open");
    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["update A-1"]);
  });

  it("no write for a record that was read and not changed", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    await orders.require("A-1");
    await orders.require("A-2");

    expect(uow.plan()).toHaveLength(0);
    await uow.commit();
    expect(store.applied).toBe(0);
  });

  it("one insert carrying every change made to a new record", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const added = orders.add({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });
    change(added, { total: 7 });

    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["insert A-9"]);
    await uow.commit();

    expect(stored(store, "A-9")?.total).toBe(7);
  });

  it("nothing for a record added and then removed", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const added = orders.add({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });
    added.remove();

    expect(uow.plan()).toHaveLength(0);
    await uow.commit();
    expect(store.applied).toBe(0);
    expect(store.records(spec)).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("a delete and nothing else for a record changed and then removed", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    change(order, { total: 999 });
    order.remove();

    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["delete A-1"]);
    await uow.commit();
    expect(store.records(spec)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("one delete however many times a record is removed", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    order.remove();
    order.remove();

    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["delete A-1"]);
  });

  it("inserts, then updates, then deletes, in the order they were registered", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const first = await orders.require("A-1");
    first.remove();
    orders.add({
      id: "A-8",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });
    const second = await orders.require("A-2");
    change(second, { total: 5 });
    orders.add({
      id: "A-7",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });

    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual([
      "insert A-8",
      "insert A-7",
      "update A-2",
      "delete A-1",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("what the transaction sees of itself", () => {
  it("one handle for a record loaded twice", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const first = await orders.require("A-1");
    const second = await orders.require("A-1");

    expect(first).toBe(second);
    change(first, { total: 42 });
    expect(totalOf(second)).toBe(42);
    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["update A-1"]);
  });

  it("a record added is found by load, without the store being read", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { orders } = opened(store);

    const added = orders.add({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });

    expect(await orders.load("A-9")).toBe(added);
  });

  it("a record removed reads as absent", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    order.remove();

    expect(await orders.load("A-1")).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe("what it refuses", () => {
  it("a key it is already tracking", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { orders } = opened(store);

    await orders.require("A-1");

    expect(
      refusalFrom(() => {
        orders.add({
          id: "A-1",
          total: 1,
          status: "open",
          shipping: { city: "Hull" },
        });
      }),
    ).toBeInstanceOf(AlreadyTrackedError);
  });

  it("a record that has to exist and does not", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { orders } = opened(store);

    await expect(orders.require("A-404")).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      RecordNotFoundError,
    );
    expect(await orders.load("A-404")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("everything, once it has been committed", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    change(order, { total: 1 });
    await uow.commit();

    await expect(uow.commit()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(UnitOfWorkClosedError);
    await expect(orders.load("A-2")).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      UnitOfWorkClosedError,
    );
    expect(
      refusalFrom(() => {
        orders.add({
          id: "A-9",
          total: 1,
          status: "open",
          shipping: { city: "Hull" },
        });
      }),
    ).toBeInstanceOf(UnitOfWorkClosedError);
    expect(
      refusalFrom(() => {
        order.remove();
      }),
    ).toBeInstanceOf(UnitOfWorkClosedError);
  });

  it("a change to a record that was removed", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    order.remove();

    expect(
      refusalFrom(() => {
        change(order, { total: 1 });
      }),
    ).toBeInstanceOf(RemovedRecordError);
  });
});

describe("what a change is", () => {
  it("a patch merges rather than replacing", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    order.update({ total: 7 });
    order.update({ status: "paid" });

    expect(totalOf(order)).toBe(7);
    expect(statusOf(order)).toBe("paid");
    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["update A-1"]);
  });

  it("an undefined value is not a change, and does not erase the field", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    // What a caller reaches for when a form field was left blank. Erasing a
    // field has to be said in the domain type — with a null, or an
    // absent-marker of its own — because a `Partial` cannot tell "leave it
    // alone" from "clear it".
    order.update({ total: undefined });

    expect(uow.plan()).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(totalOf(order)).toBe(100);
  });

  it("an empty patch is not a change", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    order.update({});

    expect(uow.plan()).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

describe("one transaction, or none of it", () => {
  it("an abandoned transaction writes nothing", async () => {
    const store = seeded();

    await expect(
      withUnitOfWork(store, async (uow) => {
        const order = await orders<Order>(uow).require("A-1");
        change(order, { status: "paid" });
        throw new Error("a domain rule said no");
      }),
    ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(Error);

    expect(store.applied).toBe(0);
    expect(stored(store, "A-1")?.status).toBe("open");
  });

  it("a commit that fails leaves the unit of work open", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    // A key the store holds and this unit of work never loaded, so only the
    // store can refuse it.
    orders.add({
      id: "A-1",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });

    await expect(uow.commit()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(AlreadyStoredError);
    expect(planOf(uow)).toEqual(["insert A-1"]);
    expect(store.records(spec)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(store.applied).toBe(0);

    // Still usable, which is the whole claim: nothing was written, so the
    // caller can look at what happened and decide. A unit of work closed by a
    // failure would swallow this.
    expect(await orders.require("A-2")).toBeDefined();
  });

  it("a commit that succeeded has nothing left to do", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const kept = await orders.require("A-1");
    change(kept, { total: 7 });
    const gone = await orders.require("A-2");
    gone.remove();
    orders.add({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });
    await uow.commit();

    // `plan` is the one method a closed unit of work still answers, so it has
    // to answer truthfully: every accumulated change has been written and none
    // of it is pending.
    expect(uow.plan()).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(store.applied).toBe(1);
  });

  it("a conflict names the record, and nothing in the batch is written", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-1");
    change(order, { total: 999 });
    orders.add({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 1,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });

    // Somebody else commits first.
    await store.apply([
      {
        kind: "update",
        collection: ORDERS_COLLECTION,
        key: "A-1",
        record: {
          id: "A-1",
          total: 101,
          status: "open",
          shipping: { city: "York" },
          version: 2,
        },
        expectedVersion: 1,
      },
    ]);

    await expect(uow.commit()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ConcurrencyError);
    expect(stored(store, "A-9")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("a committed record carries the version that was stored", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    const order = await orders.require("A-2");
    change(order, { total: 41 });
    await uow.commit();

    expect(stored(store, "A-2")?.version).toBe(8);
    // The record still in hand agrees, so its next write will not conflict for
    // no reason.
    expect(order.value.version).toBe(8);
    expect(order.value.version).toBeGreaterThan(7);
  });

  it("a new record is inserted with everything it was given and a version of one", async () => {
    const store = seeded();
    const { uow, orders } = opened(store);

    orders.add({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 3,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
    });
    await uow.commit();

    expect(stored(store, "A-9")).toEqual({
      id: "A-9",
      total: 3,
      status: "open",
      shipping: { city: "Hull" },
      version: 1,
    });
  });
});
```
